subhead: Take a free practice quiz or point your phone at any Nutrition exam question for an instant, explained answer — macros, micros, and metabolism demystified, without the guesswork.
metaDescription: Free Nutrition quiz and practice questions with instant, explained answers. Macronutrients, micronutrients, dietary guidelines, and metabolism basics.
whyItWorks: Intro nutrition courses mix hard science (metabolic pathways, nutrient functions) with shifting public guidelines, and questions often hinge on a specific number or exception. Cambo explains not just the right answer but the reasoning behind the recommendation, so the numbers actually stick.

sampleQuestions.q: Which macronutrient provides the most calories per gram?
sampleQuestions.a: Fat provides about 9 calories per gram, more than double the roughly 4 calories per gram provided by carbohydrates or protein.

sampleQuestions.q: Which vitamin is primarily synthesized by the skin when exposed to sunlight?
sampleQuestions.a: Vitamin D — UV exposure triggers a reaction in the skin that converts a cholesterol derivative into an active form of the vitamin.

sampleQuestions.q: What is the primary function of dietary fiber?
options: Aids digestion and promotes bowel regularity
sampleQuestions.a: Fiber isn't digested or absorbed — it adds bulk to stool and supports regular digestion, and soluble fiber also helps moderate blood sugar and cholesterol.

sampleQuestions.q: Which mineral deficiency is most commonly associated with iron-deficiency anemia?
sampleQuestions.a: Iron — it's essential for making hemoglobin, the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen; too little leads to fatigue and anemia.

sampleQuestions.q: According to general dietary guidelines, which nutrient should make up the largest portion of a balanced plate?
sampleQuestions.a: Fruits and vegetables — most current guidelines recommend they fill about half of a balanced plate, alongside grains and protein.

options: The calories burned during vigorous exercise
The minimum energy the body needs at complete rest to sustain basic functions
The total calories consumed in a day
The rate at which food moves through the digestive tract
sampleQuestions.a: BMR is the energy the body needs at rest just to keep vital functions like breathing and circulation running — it typically makes up the largest share of total daily calorie needs.

faqs.q: What does an intro Nutrition course typically cover?
faqs.a: Macronutrients (carbs, protein, fat), micronutrients (vitamins and minerals), digestion and metabolism, energy balance, and how dietary guidelines apply across the lifespan.

faqs.q: What's the difference between macronutrients and micronutrients?
faqs.a: Macronutrients (carbohydrates, protein, and fat) are needed in large amounts and provide energy; micronutrients (vitamins and minerals) are needed in small amounts and support specific body functions.

There's a fair amount of memorizing specific nutrients and their functions, but most exams also test whether you can apply that knowledge to a scenario, like identifying a deficiency from a set of symptoms.

faqs.q: Is Cambo affiliated with any university?
faqs.a: No. Cambo is an independent study tool and isn't produced, endorsed, or affiliated with any college or university.

faqs.q: How is Nutrition different from a full dietetics program?
faqs.a: An intro Nutrition gen-ed course covers foundational science and guidelines for a general audience, while a dietetics program goes much deeper into clinical application, medical nutrition therapy, and counseling — usually as part of a dedicated major.

faqs.q: Can Cambo help with a nutrient-tracking or meal-planning assignment?
faqs.a: Cambo is built for practice questions and explanations, not diet tracking — but it can help you understand the concepts (like reading a nutrition label or calculating macronutrient percentages) behind that kind of assignment.
